hypotheses.reasoning: Redis was swapped onto a replacement node and came back with an empty cache (no RDB snapshot) at 20:08:17 (#68). The order-service miss ratio then jumped from 2% to 95% (#69), so it sent every read straight to postgres. That cache stampede filled postgres connections (491/500) and pushed CPU to 94-98% (#74, #79). Point lookups by id slowed to 2.5-8s (#75, #99, #114), order-service queries timed out after 5s (#84, #108), and the gateway returned 504s (#78 onward). Before the restart, cache hits were normal and checkouts finished in about 129ms (#64, #67).
The direct cause of the timeouts is postgres running out of connections and CPU. But that saturation is a result of the cold cache, not something that started on its own.
One card-processor connection reset at 20:03:49, retry 1/3. It's isolated and comes before the onset, so it's most likely a red herring.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm the redis cache for hot order keys, or rate-limit and coalesce cache-miss reads so they don't all hit postgres at once. Briefly cap order-service DB concurrency or shed load until the hit ratio recovers. Turn on RDB/AOF persistence or replicas so that replacing a redis node doesn't bring it back empty, and add a guard against cache stampedes (request coalescing or early recompute).
